glosses: A point at which reflected or refracted rays of light converge.

examples.text: The heat of sunlight at the focus of a magnifying glass can easily set dry leaves on fire.

glosses: A point of a conic at which rays reflected from a curve or surface converge.

examples.text: Unfortunately, the license plate is out of focus in this image.

glosses: The quality of the convergence of light on the photographic medium.

examples.text: During this scene, the boy’s face shifts subtly from soft focus into sharp focus.

glosses: Something to which activity, attention or interest is primarily directed.

examples.text: My studies are my main focus right now.

glosses: The exact point of where an earthquake occurs, in three dimensions (underneath the epicentre).

examples.text: The earthquake's focus was at exactly 37 degrees north, 18 degrees south, seventy five meters below the ground.

glosses: The status of being the currently active element in a user interface, often indicated by a visual highlight.

examples.text: Text entered at the keyboard or pasted from a clipboard is sent to the component which currently has the focus.

glosses: The most important word or phrase in a sentence or passage, or the one that imparts information.
An object used in casting a magic spell.

examples.text: Candles, in fact, are an essential ingredient in many spells. They can be used as either the focus of the spell or as a component that sets the spell's overall mood and tone.

glosses: The centre of an older fish's scale, which is the point where a younger fish's scale starts to grow from.
To cause (rays of light, etc) to converge at a single point.

examples.text: The difficulties of focussing colour-light signals on curved tracks to ensure maximum sighting distance were underlined in the recent official report [...] on a low-speed collision at Newcastle Central on July 25, 1960, between an unfitted freight and a diesel-hauled passenger train.

glosses: To adjust (a lens, an optical instrument) in order to position an image with respect to the focal plane.

examples.text: You'll need to focus the microscope carefully in order to capture the full detail of this surface.

glosses: To adjust itself or be adjusted such that light from a scene converges appropriately to create a clear image.

examples.text: I can't get the lens to focus.
The camera focuses automatically on the subject's eyes.

glosses: To direct attention, effort, or energy to a particular audience or task.

examples.text: The president focused her remarks on the newcomers.
If you're going to beat your competitors, you need to focus.

glosses: To concentrate one's attention on something; to have as one's central point of interest, concern, etc.

examples.text: I have to focus on my work.

glosses: To transfer the input focus to (a visual element), so that it receives subsequent input.

examples.text: The text box won't receive the user's keystrokes unless you explicitly focus it.
